subject: history
title: Mid-Tudor Crisis: Edward VI and Mary I
welcome_lead: Track the Protestant lurch under Edward VI and the Catholic restoration under Mary I.
meta_desc: A-Level adventure on Edward VI's Protestantism 1547-53 and Mary I's Catholic restoration 1553-58.
final_note: You can now assess whether the 'mid-Tudor crisis' label is justified.

concepts.def: Edward Seymour's rule 1547-49 as Lord Protector for Edward VI, ended by political failure and the 1549 rebellions.
Cranmer's liturgy, moderately Protestant, imposed by the Act of Uniformity 1549; triggered the Prayer Book Rebellion.
Sharply Protestant revision rejecting the real presence; symbol of Edward's reformation.
Protestant claimant proclaimed queen for nine days in July 1553 by Northumberland; executed 1554.
Mary I's 1553-58 reversal of Edwardian reform: restoring the Mass, papal authority (Pole's reconciliation 1554) and burning ~283 Protestants.
Final English continental possession lost to France in January 1558, a blow to Marian prestige.

walkthroughs.body_html: Edward VI (1547-53) was a minor; Somerset ruled as Protector until 1549. The 1549 Act of Uniformity imposed the First Prayer Book, prompting the Prayer Book Rebellion (West Country) and Kett's Rebellion (Norfolk, agrarian). Northumberland (Dudley) ousted Somerset and from 1550 drove further reform: the 1552 Prayer Book, the Forty-Two Articles (1553) and the dissolution of chantries.

Mary defeated Lady Jane Grey's coup in July 1553 with popular support. The First Statute of Repeal (1553) undid Edward's religious laws; the Second Statute of Repeal (1554) restored papal authority. Cardinal Reginald Pole reconciled England to Rome in November 1554. The Marian persecutions burned approximately 283 Protestants 1555-58, including Cranmer, Ridley and Latimer, immortalised by Foxe's Acts and Monuments.

Mary's 1554 marriage to Philip of Spain alarmed Protestants and provoked Wyatt's Rebellion (January-February 1554). Drawn into Habsburg war with France, England lost Calais in January 1558, held since 1347. Mary died in November 1558 without an heir.
